blocks.orig: You and your besties are always on the lookout for new adventures? Then get ready for big smiles and eyes, because Tanzania has just that for you… plus a stunning flora and fauna… plus a mesmerizing culture… plus music, dance, and party.
blocks.html: Are you and your best friends forever hunting for the next adventure? Then prepare for wide eyes and even wider smiles, because Tanzania delivers exactly that… plus spectacular flora and fauna… plus a captivating culture… plus music, dancing and parties.

blocks.orig: If you’re adventurous, you can climb the famous Kilimanjaro, dive into the unique national parks during breathtaking safaris and go swimming with whale sharks on Mafia Island (don’t worry, they’re vegan).
blocks.html: Looking for thrills? You can climb the famous Kilimanjaro, plunge into the extraordinary national parks on jaw-dropping safaris and swim with whale sharks off Mafia Island (relax, they’re vegan).

blocks.orig: If you fancy a tad more relaxation and luxury during your holiday, simply pick lodges that pamper you after your safari (yes, you have to do one!). Heck, you could even fly from one highlight to the next instead of drive!
blocks.html: Prefer a touch more relaxation and luxury on your holiday? Then simply choose lodges that spoil you once the safari is done (and yes, a safari is compulsory!). You could even hop between highlights by plane rather than by car!

blocks.orig: And should you want to enjoy the Tanzanian nightlife, simply head over to Stone Town or Jambiani on Zanzibar, where history is beautifully combined with relaxing beach days, beach fires and beach parties.
blocks.html: And if a taste of Tanzanian nightlife is what you are after, make your way to Stone Town or Jambiani on Zanzibar, where history blends beautifully with lazy beach days, beach fires and beach parties.

blocks.orig: Whatever you prefer to do, discovering Tanzania with your friends will be a memory that will connect you forever.
blocks.html: Whichever way you choose to do it, exploring Tanzania together with your friends creates a memory that will bind you for life.

blocks.orig: When in Tanzania, you have to put a safari on your itinerary. You simply have to. Witness the Great Migration in the world-famous Serengeti, explore the depths of the Ngorongoro Crater, or discover the hidden beauties of the lesser-known Ruaha National Park. Tanzania is home to several national parks, you just have to pick your faves. And wherever you end up going on a safari, remember: hold your friends close, and your camera closer 😉
blocks.html: A safari belongs on every Tanzania itinerary. There is no way around it. See the Great Migration in the world-famous Serengeti, descend into the Ngorongoro Crater, or uncover the hidden gems of the lesser-known Ruaha National Park. With so many national parks in Tanzania, all you need to do is choose your favourites. And wherever your safari takes you, remember: keep your friends close and your camera closer 😉

blocks.orig: Should you have been flirting with the idea of going to Arusha, the Wildlife Residence might just be perfect for you and your friends. This charming and environmentally-friendly lodge has it all: golf and polo with a view on the Kilimanjaro and Mount Meru, horse safaris among zebras, wildebeests, elands and the rare gerenuks, sundowners on the terrace. Sounds perfect? That’s because it is!
blocks.html: If Arusha has been on your mind, the Wildlife Residence could be just right for you and your friends. This charming, eco-friendly lodge offers the lot: golf and polo with Kilimanjaro and Mount Meru in view, horse safaris among zebras, wildebeest, elands and the rare gerenuk, and sundowners on the terrace. Sounds too good? It really is that good!

blocks.orig: No matter if you’re a travel influencer or not – this instagrammable wonder of nature is a must-see! Located between Arusha and Moshi, the crystal blue water of these springs is almost too beautiful to be true. Relax in this natural gem, take countless pictures in, at and under the water and swing into it with some ropes. This is fabby fun at its finest!
blocks.html: Travel influencer or not, this instagrammable natural wonder deserves a place on your list! Found between Arusha and Moshi, these springs have water so crystal blue it hardly seems real. Unwind in this natural gem, snap endless photos in, beside and beneath the water, and swing in on the ropes. Fabby fun doesn’t get better than this!

blocks.orig: The Maasai are probably one of the most-famous tribes in the world, and of course you can go and visit them in their homes. If you want to take your cultural experience up a notch, go hunting with the Hadzabe. However, we have to warn you: this is not for the faint-hearted, since you might see animals get shot by arrows. Still, being part of this unique tribe and getting to know their customs and click language is a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
blocks.html: The Maasai must be among the best-known tribes anywhere, and you can of course visit them at home. To take the cultural experience a step further, go hunting with the Hadzabe. A word of warning, though: this is not for the squeamish, as you may see animals being shot with arrows. Even so, joining this unique tribe and learning about their customs and click language is something you will experience only once in your life.

blocks.orig: Those who want to learn even more about the Hadzabe and neighboring Datooga tribe can even opt for an overnight camping experience in their territory. During the day you venture into the wilderness with a few members of the tribe, in the evening you gather around a campfire. You all share a yummy meal and fun stories and fall asleep under the stars. The tents are simply made of mosquito netting, but pamper you with proper duvets and mattresses 😉
blocks.html: If you want to go deeper still into the world of the Hadzabe and the neighbouring Datooga tribe, you can even spend a night camping on their land. By day you head out into the wilderness with a few tribe members; in the evening everyone sits around the campfire, shares a tasty meal and fun stories, and drifts off to sleep under the stars. The tents are no more than mosquito netting, yet they come with proper duvets and mattresses 😉

blocks.orig: No matter if you’re an experienced diver or on-holiday-snorkeller: swimming with whale sharks is an adventure for anyone. On Mafia Island you can go deep from November to March and meet these gentle giants of the sea in their natural habitat, a truly humbling experience. And should you want to see more, you can also snorkel along the beautiful coral reefs of the island’s marine park or simply keep your eyes open for humpback whales swimming along the coast.
blocks.html: Seasoned diver or holiday snorkeller, it makes no difference: swimming with whale sharks is an adventure for everyone. From November to March you can dive off Mafia Island and encounter these gentle giants of the sea in their own habitat, a genuinely humbling moment. Want more? Snorkel along the island’s lovely coral reefs in the marine park, or keep a lookout for humpback whales passing along the coast.

blocks.orig: These are just some of countless activities waiting for you in Tanzania. From hot air balloon safaris to treetop walks and sunset cruises – check out all activities here… after finishing this article, of course 😉
blocks.html: And these are only a few of the countless things to do in Tanzania. From hot-air balloon safaris to treetop walks and sunset cruises – browse all activities here… once you have finished reading this article, naturally 😉

blocks.orig: This historical capital of Zanzibar is known for its vibrant atmosphere, live concerts and amazing rooftop bars and restaurants. However, it also has a rich heritage and is filled with little shops and markets that want to be explored. Around sunset, the city truly comes to life. Enjoy your sundowner(s) on the rooftops of Emerson Spice, Upendo House or the Taarab Restaurant on top of DoubleTree by Hilton Zanzibar and grab a market-style snack at the Forodhani Gardens. You can also start your evening by watching the locals somersaulting into the ocean before enjoying your dinner.
blocks.html: The historic capital of Zanzibar is famous for its lively vibe, live concerts and superb rooftop bars and restaurants. At the same time it has a rich heritage and is packed with small shops and markets waiting to be explored. As the sun goes down the city really wakes up. Have your sundowner(s) on the rooftops of Emerson Spice, Upendo House or the Taarab Restaurant atop the DoubleTree by Hilton Zanzibar, and pick up a market-style bite at the Forodhani Gardens. Before dinner you could also watch the locals somersaulting into the sea.

blocks.orig: Our tip: the Livingstone Bar. Located directly at the beach, you can sip your sundowners (half price!) with your feet in the sand, listen to live music and watch acrobats and locals dancing at sunset.
blocks.html: Our recommendation: the Livingstone Bar. Right on the beach, it lets you enjoy half-price sundowners with your toes in the sand, live music in your ears and acrobats and locals dancing as the sun sets.

blocks.orig: Traditional and contemporary African music played live in an old fort in the middle of Stone Town. This is Sauti za Busara, an amazing festival that takes place every year in February. So plan your holiday accordingly and book your tickets early for what might be the most incredible little festival you will ever attend!
blocks.html: Live traditional and modern African music in an old fort right in the heart of Stone Town: that is Sauti za Busara, a wonderful festival held each February. Plan your holiday around it and get your tickets early, because this may well be the most amazing little festival you ever go to!

blocks.orig: These two villages in the East of Zanzibar are your go-to-locations (literally) if you want to experience the true tropical beach life. With plenty of little restaurants, bars and resorts, there is always party or live music to be found. During the day, you can just relax at the pool or have fun together at some watersports activity. You could also go for a bike ride, on a spice tour or visit the Kua Cave. And of course you can go snorkelling, bask in the sun and swim in the glistening sea.
blocks.html: For real tropical beach life, these two villages on Zanzibar’s east coast are (quite literally) the places to go. With lots of small restaurants, bars and resorts, a party or live music is never far away. By day you can laze by the pool or try a watersport together. A bike ride, a spice tour or a visit to the Kua Cave are other options. And naturally there is snorkelling, sunbathing and swimming in the sparkling sea.

blocks.orig: The best lounge spot in the middle of Paje: relax directly at the beach, jump into the pool and share one of the simple rooms with your buddies. If you crave something more luxurious, there are also some beautifully designed lofts to sleep in. And of course they serve coffee (“kagawa” is Swahili for “coffee”), for those lazy hot mornings that follow the cool and joyous tropical nights.
blocks.html: The finest spot to lounge in the heart of Paje: chill right on the beach, dive into the pool and share one of the simple rooms with your mates. Fancy something more upmarket? There are gorgeously designed lofts to sleep in as well. And they serve coffee, of course (“kagawa” means “coffee” in Swahili), for those slow, hot mornings after the cool, joyful tropical nights.

blocks.orig: If you’re lucky enough to be in Zanzibar during a full moon, you cannot miss out on the Kendwa Full Moon Party. Right on the beach, this party is livened up by DJs, a beautiful crowd and a great atmosphere. What an ending (or beginning) to another unforgettable holiday with your BFFs 😉
blocks.html: Should you happen to be on Zanzibar at full moon, the Kendwa Full Moon Party is not to be missed. Held right on the beach, it comes alive with DJs, a beautiful crowd and a fantastic atmosphere. What a way to end (or begin) yet another unforgettable holiday with your BFFs 😉
